# Surgical Outcomes

This folder contains clinical quality indicators from the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) that evaluate treatment speed, logistical efficiency, and post-operative mortality in acute surgical care. The indicators track critical time-sensitive metrics, such as the time to CT scanning and the speed of operative intervention for life-threatening conditions and ileus. Additionally, the folder includes supplementary mortality indicators that stratify 30-day survival outcomes by the patients' Charlson Comorbidity Index scores. Together, these pages provide a risk-adjusted framework for comparing hospital performance and ensuring high-quality acute care across Denmark's healthcare system.

## Pages

- [[indikator-10b|Indikator 10b]] — Measures 30-day post-operative mortality for acute surgery patients with a moderate comorbidity burden (Charlson Score 1 or 2).
- [[indikator-10c|Indikator 10c]] — Tracks 30-day mortality for high-risk acute surgery patients with a Charlson Score of 3 or higher.
- [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] — Evaluates diagnostic speed by measuring the proportion of patients receiving a CT scan within two hours of hospital arrival.
- [[indikator-4x|Indikator 4x]] — Monitors the speed of acute surgical intervention for life-threatening conditions like perforation, ischemia, or postoperative bleeding, targeting operation within six hours.
- [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]] — Measures the proportion of patients undergoing ileus surgery without ischemia or perforation who are operated on within 24 hours of arrival.
- [[indikator-9b|Indikator 9b]] — Provides regional and hospital-level breakdowns of 30-day mortality for patients with a Charlson Score of 1 or 2.
- [[indikator-9c|Indikator 9c]] — Details regional and hospital-level 30-day mortality outcomes for high-risk patients with a Charlson Score of 3 or higher.
